mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 5% over a two-month window signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and cost-push inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 5% in last 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint signal does not outperform a single-variable model at the 5% significance level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over one month indicates a paradoxical labor market signal (e.g., underemployment), which reduces effective labor productivity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the interaction signal is not statistically distinct from either single-variable signal.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumer spending momentum, which depresses retail and discretionary sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising household income growth.
